findings.passage: “What we’re doing is buying time and hopefully gaining attention on this issue. What we really need is for Congress to act.”
findings.note: Quoted by the Associated Press (via Press Herald) as Wu left Texas to deny a quorum on the 2021 special-session voting bill (SB 1). Wu is also reported as saying the bill would restrict voting, especially in minority and poor communities. Does not discuss ID rules directly.

findings.passage: "We started out this special session with promises that there would be compromises there, that there would be changes to the bill and that they would work with us. After a 24-hour hearing almost 500 witnesses testified overwhelmingly in opposition. Ten to one in opposition. They just voted it all out. All efforts to make things a little bit better, were rejected without question," said Wu.
findings.note: Fox 26 Houston quoted Wu as he left for Washington to block the 2021 voting bill (SB 1, which also added ID numbers for mail ballots). He criticizes how the committee handled amendments and witness testimony; he does not name ID rules.
